messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis  
Details:  
The failing test `testFileValidator()` adds a `FileValidator` instance to an argument of an option, then tries to parse command line arguments specifying an existing file path. The reported failure is a `ClassCastException` stating that `java.io.File` cannot be cast to `java.lang.String`.  

Analysis of the `Parser.parseAndHelp()` shows it internally calls `parse()`. The `parse()` method prepares a list of input arguments as strings, creates a `WriteableCommandLineImpl` for the group (collection of options/arguments), and calls `group.process()`.  

The `GroupImpl.process()` iterates over input strings, matches them to known options or anonymous arguments, and calls the corresponding `Option.process()`. The `Option.process()` implementation (in `ParentImpl.process()`) processes the argument if it exists by calling `argument.processValues()`.  

Looking at `ArgumentImpl.processValues()`, it reads and consumes argument strings from the iterator and calls `WriteableCommandLineImpl.addValue()` to add parsed values.  

`WriteableCommandLineImpl.addValue()` stores values in a map keyed by Options. Critically, `addValue()` accepts an `Object` as the value, meaning `FileValidator` has been successfully converting a String input into a `File` object (likely via validation logic). This means `addValue()` receives a `File` instance rather than a String.  

The test and bug report indicate the main issue: somewhere later in the parsing or in application code, the parsed value for the `--file-name` option is assumed to be a String, but here it is actually a `File` instance. When this assumption manifests as a cast `(String)` on the value, it throws `ClassCastException`.  

The root cause is a mismatch between argument value types expected by the client code (String) versus the actual object type returned by `FileValidator` (File). The parsing framework allows storing any Object, but downstream code or the CLI framework likely blindly casts values to String assuming no transformation happened. The test fails because the validated Argument stores a File instance, causing this ClassCastException when the parser result is used.  

No evidence from recent bug reports indicates related or similar problems, so they do not provide additional insight.  

In summary: The bug occurs because `FileValidator` converts the argument value to a File object, but downstream code or the `CommandLine` API assumes it is a String, causing a ClassCastException during cast operations. The root fix would involve either the parser/CommandLine API handling non-string argument values properly or adjusting assumptions/casts in consuming code.  

Next, I will identify the best methods for fixing this issue.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
